items.gist: The passage presents the dvādaśānta triśūla and devīcakra as a powerful emanative structure whose realization leads to khecarī attainment.
It directs worship of individual devīs or mantras in the lotus, with distinctions of real and unreal.
After making one's consciousness Śiva through internal worship, one should perform the external rite.
External worship is primary for siddhi and related aims, while internal worship purifies the worshipper; one without siddhi-interest worships externally for internal mahāyāga.
After internal worship, one casts mantra-empowered substances in directions and performs purification saṃskāras such as inspection, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and veiling.
The text prescribes pañcagavya substances and kuśa water for purification, distinguishing external impurity from internal impurity.
Mantra and related elements burn impurity, while flowers, incense, perfumes, and other offerings are placed in the fire.
The whole deity circle is established in the mandala, and Gaṇeśa is worshipped and dismissed for obstacle removal.
The kumbha is filled, worshipped, and mantra-empowered, then placed in the northeast and used for worship of directional lords.
The disciple pours from the kumbha while the guru guides the rite, and the kumbha is placed in the northeast with directional mantras.
Mantra groups are strengthened in the kumbha, and the astra is worshipped in the karkarī for obstacle removal.
The text prepares the kuṇḍa and declares this saṃskāra supreme, applicable in body, ground, liṅga, vessel, water, and other supports.
All ordinary acts become worship for the ripe practitioner, while a gradual rite is prescribed for those not yet established in that awareness.
The practitioner identifies as Śiva and mantra, and gradual competence is compared to learning speech through practice.
The passage enumerates kuṇḍa construction, covering, lines, protection, and the establishment of Śakti for removing obstacles.
Mātṛkā or Mālinī is installed in the kuṇḍa, and offerings are made with the five limbs after the fire is established.
The fire becomes purified through all saṃskāras, and the fire is identified with Śiva through Śiva-saṃkalpa.
The text rejects endless saṃskāra regress and directs worship of the parents and pure abode after the fire is purified.
A portion of purified fire is taken, and the tattvas are purified through the saṃskāra process.

items.topic: Śiva fire oblation and tattva vision
items.gist: Oblations are offered to Śiva fire, and the tattva vision is said to be the life of saṃskāra.
The passage concludes with sruva and related implements, tarpāṇa, and homa according to means, ending with a warning about external predominance.
